Photograph: Al-Arab in UK West Sussex Couple who died with their daughter off Sussex coast named by police Officers still investigating deaths of Zeina Alayn, Hassan El-Khawas and daughter Sara El-Khawas at Shoreham-by-Sea Matthew Weaver Wed 19 Aug 2026 13.48 EDT First published on Wed 19 Aug 2026 08.45 EDT Share Prefer the Guardian on Google A father, mother and their teenage daughter who died off the Sussex coast on Tuesday have been identified. Sussex police named the victims as Hassan El-Khawas, 55, his partner, Zeina Alayn, 37, and their 14-year-old daughter, Sara El-Khawas. A younger girl who was also part of the family is in hospital in a critical condition. She has not been named. The Palestinian embassy in London said El-Khawas was a British man of Palestinian descent. Police, paramedics, coastguard crews and a lifeboat attended the scene at Shoreham-by-Sea, where four people were pulled from the water. Sussex police said the cause of the tragedy was still being investigated. It could not confirm reports that the older girl got caught in a fishing net. The force said in a statement: “Following review of CCTV footage and initial witness accounts, the current hypothesis is that this was a tragic accident, with no third-party involvement.” Adnan Hmidan, the chair of the Palestinian Forum in Britain, said: “According to the information available to us, the family encountered strong currents while at sea. Their daughter, Sara, became caught in a fishing net and her father attempted to help free her. “As the waves and currents intensified, her mother, Zeina, also entered the water to try to save them, followed by their younger daughter.” View image in fullscreen A woman lays flowers in memory of the three family members on the beach at Shoreham-by-Sea. Photograph: Yui Mok/PA Two other children from the family were in the care of their paternal uncle, he said. “The Khawas family are British citizens of Palestinian origin, with roots in Rashidieh refugee camp in Lebanon,” he said. “Like many Palestinian families, members of their extended family have lived in Britain for many years and have built a strong and close-knit community here. “Our thoughts and prayers are with the entire family, particularly the children, who are facing an unimaginable loss. We ask everyone to respect their privacy and dignity at this painful time.” Andy Burnham said the incident was “a terrible family tragedy” and a reminder of the dangers of open water swimming. There was a huge emergency service response to the incident on Tuesday afternoon, when police were told four people had got into difficulty in the water. Sussex police said they believed all four entered the water to swim. Ch Supt James Collis confirmed that a man, woman and a teenage girl had died at the scene. View image in fullscreen Two air ambulance helicopters and a critical care team were sent to the scene and Shoreham RNLI said its lifeboat had been called out at 3pm. Photograph: Jamie Lashmar/PA Asked if the government needed to do more on water safety, Burnham said: “Always. It’s so sad to hear what happened yesterday, and obviously we think there’s a young girl still in the hospital fighting for her life, and we send our best wishes and love to wider friends and family. But a real tragedy, a real terrible family tragedy.” Speaking on a visit to north-east England, Burnham added: “Obviously, we will look in detail at what happened. The thing I can say today, and there is still, I think, a further heatwave to come in this summer period, it is just to remind people about the dangers of open-water swimming. The coldness, even when it feels hot outside, it can shock people, and that can cause the difficulties. So people just need to remember that at all times.” Two air ambulance helicopters and a critical care team were sent to the scene and Shoreham RNLI said its lifeboat had been called out at 3pm. Burnham paid tribute to those who tried to save the family. “I do need to praise the emergency services, who I know were on scene very quickly yesterday. They’ve had a busy summer, but they were there, and we thank them. As I say, just huge sympathy to the friends and the family,” he said. View image in fullscreen A note left among the floral tributes on Shoreham-by-Sea beach. Photograph: Yui Mok/PA There have been a series of water-related deaths across the country in a summer of record-breaking heat. On Saturday, a 12-year-old boy drowned in the River Lea, near Hackney Marshes in north-east London. In April, a woman and her young child died after getting into difficulty in the water in west London. Both died at the scene in Elthorne Park, Ealing, the Metropolitan police said. There have been at least 35 drowning deaths, including eight in July, according to a study by the London School of Hygiene & Tropical Medicine. Joss Loader, the chair of Shoreham Beach Residents’ Association, said: “There’s just a really strong sense of shock, obviously people are really concerned for the young girl. A small, tightly knit community with a very deep sense of shock and that sense of disbelief you get after a tragedy because it has come out of nowhere.” Shoreham beach is a spit of land with water on three sides from the River Adur, the estuary and the sea, and Loader said she understood the “tragic events” had happened in the estuary. “It’s school holidays and we have had a wonderful summer so the beaches have been packed with families,” she said. “People swim from those beaches even in the winter, generally it is considered as safe as the sea can be. You wouldn’t be swimming there and think you were taking a risk.” Anna Peacock, 81, who lives near Kingston beach across the water from Shoreham Fort, said emergency services were on the scene very quickly. “People come down to swim, particularly in the summertime and I don’t think they realise there’s a riptide along here,” she said. “It’s very inviting to come to the sea, but the tide could carry you out in seconds, and I don’t think people have realised that.” Explore more on these topics West Sussex news Share Reuse this content Most viewed Most viewed UK UK politics Education Media Society Law Scotland Wales Northern Ireland

https://www.finanznachrichten.de/nachric.text: Westinghouse Electric Company: PEJ and Westinghouse Begin Long-Lead Item Procurement Process for Poland's First Nuclear Power Plant Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe (PEJ) has commissioned Westinghouse Electric Company to begin procuring long-lead items (LLIs) for the first AP1000 unit of the Lubiatowo-Kopalino nuclear power plant project. This is one of the most important stages in preparing for the start of construction and ensuring that the project is completed on schedule. "This is an extremely important moment for the entire project. Securing long-lead items is of direct significance for the construction schedule of Poland's first nuclear power plant. We want energy from the first reactor to reach our power outlets in 2036. This is a strategic project by the Polish government that will meet our needs for decades to come, becoming one of the cornerstones of our country's energy security," said Milosz Motyka, Minister of Energy "Thanks to the agreement reached in September between PEJ and the Consortium on the main commercial terms of the EPC contract, we are now ready to take the next step, namely begin the process of ordering long-lead items. We adopted this approach in order to give ourselves time for further detailed negotiations on the EPC contract, without the pressure that the lack of an LLI order would affect the project schedule. A sound contract that appropriately balances liability and establishes cooperation mechanisms for the construction phase is key to the project's future success," said Wojciech Wrochna, Secretary of State at the Ministry of Energy and the Government Plenipotentiary for Strategic Energy Infrastructure. The scope of orders covers six key components of the nuclear island, including the reactor containment vessel and its associated structural modules. LLIs are among the most technologically advanced and complex components of a nuclear power plant, the production and delivery of which requires many years and the involvement of specialized suppliers that meet the highest quality and safety standards. "In nuclear projects, proper preparation and effective time management are crucial. We have already ordered the first long-lead items for which Bechtel is responsible, and we are now beginning this process for Westinghouse, which is responsible for the nuclear portion of the power plant in the broadest sense. In this way, we safeguard not only the project schedule but also its budget. The components we order account for a significant part of our costs, so starting the process well in advance allows us to better control our expenses in the coming years," said Marek Woszczyk, President of the Management Board of Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe Beginning the procurement process of long-lead items early is a common practice in nuclear projects around the world. It helps ensure the availability of production capacity, minimizes the risk of delays and supports the timely completion of projects. The scope of work includes preparing technical documentation, quality and supervision plans, selecting and contracting suppliers, as well as placing orders for the materials needed to begin production. The production and delivery of finished components to the construction site will be carried out as part of a subsequent order that PEJ plans to issue under the contract for the construction of the power plant. "The ordering of long-lead items is a key milestone for this important project and helps to ensure it remains on schedule. Even more importantly, this is a critical first step for Polish industry to furnish nuclear-grade components for the plant and maximize its participation in Poland and in future AP1000 projects in Europe, " said Dan Lipman, President of Global Business Initiatives, Westinghouse. The initiation of the procurement process for components with long-lead times is part of the current Engineering Development Agreement between PEJ and the Westinghouse-Bechtel consortium PEJ and Westinghouse expect that Polish companies will bid for the contracts, provided they successfully complete the process of obtaining the ASME NQA-1 international quality standard. The high safety standards in the nuclear industry require that companies involved in the most specialized work meet stringent technical and quality requirements. This will be another step toward building domestic capabilities and create additional export opportunities for Polish industry to enter the global AP1000 technology supply chain. The procurement of components with long-lead times is a crucial step in the preparations for the construction of Poland's first nuclear power plant. The commissioning of the first unit at the Lubiatowo-Kopalino site is scheduled for 2036. The project will be one of the cornerstones of the national energy system, providing a stable, zero-emission source of energy for Poland. About Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe Polskie Elektrownie Jadrowe sp. z o.o. is a company responsible for activities including the preparation of the investment process and acting as the investor in the project to build Poland's first nuclear power plant with a total capacity of 3.75 GWe based on safe, proven, large-scale generation III (+) pressurized water reactors (PWR), and its future operation. The Company also supports the government administration in activities aimed at the execution of the Polish Nuclear Power Programme and the development of a civil nuclear power program and the civil nuclear power sector in the Republic of Poland. For more information visit: www.pej.pl. About Westinghouse Westinghouse delivers nuclear energy the world needs to meet rising electricity demand, support growing economies, strengthen energy security and power millions of homes across five continents. The company designs and deploys advanced nuclear reactors, manufactures the fuel that powers them, maintains and modernizes operating plants and advances tomorrow's breakthroughs. Founded in 1886, the company electrified the industrial economy and pioneered nuclear power with the first commercial pressurized water reactor in 1957. Today, Westinghouse technology powers 57% of the world's nuclear power plants, maintains nearly two-thirds of the world's nuclear fleet and fuels 40% of that fleet. As the global leader in deployment of nuclear power at scale, Westinghouse has one of the largest new build pipelines in the industry. From nuclear's first chapter to its next, Westinghouse turns possibility into power.
